The best thing about it is the view. The worst thing is the price.
And you? Which one do you prefer?

People ask me which city was better, and I never know how to answer, because the honest answer is annoying. They were better at different things. The first one was cheaper, warmer and much friendlier. I knew the man at the bakery, I knew his dog, and I knew which day he made the good bread. It was also the more boring of the two, and by the third winter I could feel it. The second city is more expensive, colder and a lot less friendly. Nobody at my bakery knows my name and I doubt anybody ever will. But there is something on every night of the week, the trains work, and I am better at my job than I was, because the people around me are better at theirs. So which was better? The first one was a nicer life. The second one is a bigger one. I do not think you get both.

I want to argue with the word better, because it is doing too much work. Better at what? A car can be faster and less safe at the same time. A flat can be cheaper and further from everything. A job can pay more and cost you every Sunday. So when somebody asks me whether one thing is better than another, my first question back is always the same. Better for who, and better for which part of your life? It sounds like a way of avoiding the answer. It is the opposite. Once you finish the sentence, and I mean really finish it, cheaper than, closer to, quieter than, worse for my knees, the choice usually makes itself. And you stop arguing with people who simply want a different half of the same thing.
